english.text: Before my own father passed away, we talked about the afterlife. My father had said that at his death, his "mind" would transfer to a newborn baby on a different faraway "planet," and there, he would grow up. Despite Roman Catholic and Baptist influences, my father believed in rebirth or reincarnation and other non-Xtian ideas. In the 1970s, he read books by Tuesday Lobsang Rampa and Erich von Däniken. Also my Filipino friend Greg believes in some non-Xtian ideas, despite that he claims to be a hardcore Baptist. It is difficult for others, especially Westerners, to understand my religious stance, of being a Syncretist, chiefly Buddhist-Animist, but not discounting other belief systems, and even inclining towards Science.

text: 我自己爸爸過世之前，我哋都講過死後嘅事。我爸爸曾經講過，喺佢死嗰陣，佢嘅「心靈」會轉移到另一個遙遠嘅「星球」上嘅新生嬰兒身上，而喺嗰度，佢就會長大。儘管受到羅馬天主教同浸信會嘅影響，我爸爸相信重生或者轉世同其他非 Xtian 嘅思想。喺1970年代，佢睇咗Tuesday· 洛桑 · 蘭帕同埃里希 · 馮 · 丹尼肯嘅書。仲有我個菲律賓朋友 Greg 相信一啲非 Xtian 嘅諗法，儘管佢自稱係一個硬派浸信會教徒。其他人，特別係西方人，好難理解我嘅宗教立場，即係我係一個融合主義者，主要係佛教 - 動物主義者，但唔會折扣其他信仰體系，甚至傾向埋科學。

He, therefore, rejoices in the company of youth, he is ever in search of beauty, and gives wings to the souls of his favourites. His power far exceeds that of Jove. He commands the elements: he rules the stars: he governs the world: and even the Gods themselves are more obedient to him than your flocks are to you."

author: Davidgo5867

english.text: It's Lulu Island, 3 August 2025. After supper—green figs tender with sunlight, sweet vinegar from yesterday’s pickled jar, and reheated Alfredo—I sat on the balcony and watched the conifer. Stillness below, a street without cars, without haste. My lime water, iced, caught the light. Michael, the Franco-Danish ufologist, has been in my conversations lately. We speak of inner things: the trance of smart devices, the mind’s eye dwindling. He says cafés aren’t cafés anymore. People forget how to look, how to linger. I tell him of Arthur in Japan—how he'd stare into blank walls like a monk gazing at emptiness. Lately I ask machines to speak like poets, and they do. They mimic Elizabethan verses and the old wistful lilt of Tagalog ballads. I pick blackberries along the path to Tim Hortons. "¡Moras!" I shout like a child. My friend Mora, whose blood flows with Andes mist, would smile. Today, I bought lemons. I meant limes, but lemons are all right. / blackberry morning— / a fig's ghost on my fingers / and the street still sleeps

text: 今日係露露島，2025年8月3號。食完晚飯 — 綠色無花果喺陽光下嫩滑，尋日醃製罐入面嘅甜醋，同埋重新加熱咗嘅阿爾弗雷多 — 我坐喺陽台望住針葉樹。下面靜靜哋，一條冇車，冇急嘅街道。我嘅石灰水，冰凍嘅，捉住咗光線。法國丹麥嘅飛碟學家米高最近一直喺我嘅對話入面。我哋講緊內心嘅嘢：智能裝置嘅恍惚，心靈嘅眼睛減少。佢話咖啡館唔再係咖啡館。啲人忘記咗點樣望，點樣逗留。我同佢講日本嘅亞瑟 — — 佢點樣會好似一個僧侶噉望住空虛噉盯住空白嘅牆。最近我叫機器講嘢好似詩人噉，佢哋都係咁做。佢哋模仿伊麗莎白時代嘅詩歌同埋塔加洛歌嘅古老而令人懷念嘅歌聲。我沿住去蒂姆霍頓嘅小路摘黑莓。「莫拉斯!」我好似細路噉嗌。我朋友 Mora ，佢嘅血液流動住安第斯山脈嘅霧，會笑。今日，我買咗檸檬。我係指青檸，但係檸檬都冇問題。 / 黑莓朝早 — / 我手指上面有個無花果嘅鬼魂 / 而條街仲瞓緊覺

english.text: The history of a battle, is not unlike the history of a ball. Some individuals may recollect all the little events of which the great result is the battle won or lost, but no individual can recollect the order in which, or the exact moment at which, they occurred, which makes all the difference as to their value or importance.

author: Davidgo5867

english.text: Look again at that dot. That's here. That's home. That's us. On it everyone you love, everyone you know, everyone you ever heard of, every human being who ever was, lived out their lives. The aggregate of our joy and suffering, thousands of confident religions, ideologies, and economic doctrines, every hunter and forager, every hero and coward, every creator and destroyer of civilization, every king and peasant, every young couple in love, every mother and father, hopeful child, inventor and explorer, every teacher of morals, every corrupt politician, every "superstar," every "supreme leader," every saint and sinner in the history of our species lived there—on a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam.
